claims.text: Substrate preheating during LPBF will improve the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Substrate preheating during LPBF will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Substrate preheating reduces thermal gradients in LPBF-built high-entropy alloys.
Reduced thermal gradients decrease residual-stress accumulation.
Reducing thermal gradients and residual stresses reduces fabrication-induced defects.
Standard LPBF without substrate preheating produces noticeable thermal gradients and residual stresses in high-entropy-alloy components.
Thermal gradients and residual stresses in the baseline process are associated with dimensional deviations and microcracks.
Preheating the substrate to approximately 200°C before and during LPBF is the proposed intervention.
Reducing abrupt thermal gradients improves interlayer bonding.
Substrate preheating decreases the temperature differential between the molten pool and surrounding material.
A smaller temperature differential produces more controlled solidification and less thermal shock.
More controlled solidification and reduced thermal shock decrease shrinkage-induced distortion.
More controlled solidification and reduced thermal shock mitigate microcrack formation.
Preheated specimens will have higher tensile strength than specimens produced without preheating.
Preheated specimens will have longer fatigue life than specimens produced without preheating.
Preheated specimens will have a lower density of fabrication-induced defects than specimens produced without preheating.
The benefits of substrate preheating occur only within an optimal preheating-temperature range.
Excessively high preheating temperatures may cause unwanted microstructural changes or oxidation.
The effect of substrate preheating may vary among high-entropy-alloy compositions.
